message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will install Python dependencies, run tests and lint with a variety of Python versions
# For more information see: https://help.github.com/actions/language-and-framework-guides/using-python-with-github-actions

name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [ master, release ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ master, release ]
  workflow_dispatch:  # manually launch from GitHub actions

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: [ '3.10', '3.11', '3.12', '3.13', '3.14' ]

    steps:
    - name: Free disk space
      run: |
        sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android
        sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet
        sudo rm -rf /opt/ghc
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-python@v7
      with:
        python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml', 'requirements.txt') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ matrix.python-version }}-
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install pytest
        pip install .
        pip install .[extra]
        pip install pytest-cov
    - name: Test with pytest
      run: |
        pytest --cov=fedot -s test/unit
    - name: Codecov-coverage
      uses: codecov/codecov-action@v4
      with:
        token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
",
  "rationale": "Add pip dependency caching using actions/cache@v4. The workflow currently installs dependencies from scratch on every run across 5 Python versions. Experimental evidence (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) shows ~9% elapsed time savings from caching pip dependencies. The pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (literature) and P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE (experimental) both support this optimization. Preconditions are met: repeated dependency fetching occurs (matrix of 5 Python versions), and cache inputs (pyproject.toml, requirements.txt) are present and pinned. No contraindications apply: no existing cache exists, and cached content is immutable (pip cache). The cache key includes Python version and hash of dependency files for correctness.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "pattern:P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE"]
}

The user wants me to propose a CI optimization for the given workflow based on the evidence provided. Let me analyze the workflow and the evidence.

The workflow is a Python project that:
1. Runs on ubuntu-latest with a 30-minute timeout
2. Uses a matrix strategy with Python versions 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14
3. Has fail-fast: false
4. Steps: free disk space, checkout, setup Python, install dependencies, run tests with pytest, upload coverage to codecov

Looking at the evidence, I see several patterns:
- P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: Cache dependency downloads (has experimental evidence showing ~9% savings)
- P-LIT-FAIL-FAST: Cancel remaining matrix jobs after failure (has experimental evidence)
- P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT: Bound jobs with custom timeout (has experimental evidence showing ~27% savings)
- P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE: Share cached build dependencies (has experimental evidence showing ~9% savings)

The workflow currently:
- Does NOT have any caching for pip dependencies
- Has fail-fast: false (so it runs all matrix jobs even if one fails)
- Has a 30-minute timeout at the job level
- Installs dependencies fresh each run

Looking at the experimental evidence:
1. The first evidence (experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2) shows adding pip cache saved ~9% elapsed time
2. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern from literature also supports caching dependency downloads
3. The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern has experimental evidence showing it works (though synthetic)
4. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT has experimental evidence showing ~27% savings

For this workflow, the most applicable and evidence-supported optimizations would be:
1. Add pip caching (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE / P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE) - strong evidence from experiment showing ~9% savings
2. Consider changing fail-fast to true (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST) - but need to check if all matrix outcomes are required
3. The timeout is already set to 30 minutes, but could be optimized based on history (P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT or P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT)

Let me check the preconditions and contraindications:

For P-LIT-GHA-CACHE:
- Preconditions: "Repeated dependency fetching is measurable", "Cache inputs include lockfile and environment"
- Contraindications: "Mutable or untrusted cached content", "An equivalent cache already exists"
- The workflow has pyproject.toml and requirements.txt which can serve as cache keys
- No existing cache in the workflow

For P-LIT-FAIL-FAST:
- Preconditions: "Matrix failure makes remaining results dispensable under an explicit study policy"
- Contraindications: "Every matrix outcome is required", "Full failure diagnostics are required"
- The workflow tests multiple Python versions - typically all are required for a release, so fail-fast might not be appropriate

For P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT:
- Preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists"
- The CI history shows runs completing in ~9-11 minutes (from created_at to updated_at), well under 30 minutes
- Could potentially reduce timeout, but 30 minutes seems reasonable with headroom

The strongest evidence is for adding pip caching. The experiment shows ~9% savings, and the pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is directly applicable. The workflow has pyproject.toml which can be used for cache key.

I should propose adding pip caching using actions/cache@v4, similar to the experimental example.

Let me construct the updated workflow with the cache step added after setup-python and before install dependencies.

The decision should be APPLY with the updated workflow.
